title: The 'King of Knots': Complete 5-Step Guide to the Bowline Knot (Jam-Proof & Unties in 1 Second)
summary: The Bowline is globally recognized as the undisputed 'King of Knots' for wilderness hauling, heavy load rigging, and emergency rescue. Under severe tension, its fixed loop never slips or constricts, eliminating any danger of choking or cord damage. Even after taking tremendous strain and being soaked in mud and rain, it never jams: flexing its rear collar loop pops the friction lock and unties the entire knot in a single second. Master the timeless 4-beat mnemonic ('The Rabbit and The Tree') and full-locking sequence step by step.

materials.name: 1 Length of Durable Cordage (2m+ paracord or rope)
materials.desc: Prepare 6~8mm high-friction cordage or 550 paracord with dependable tensile strength for knot practice and heavy field rigging.

materials.name: Practice Post or Handle (Forearm-thick branch)
materials.desc: A 5~7cm diameter hardwood branch or anchor handle to test the knot under real tensile load.

steps.title: Step 1: Form the 'Rabbit Hole' Loop (Number 6 Shape) Over the Standing Line
steps.description: Hold the long standing line (the tree) and form a small palm-sized circular loop. The most critical requirement here is that the working end (the rabbit) must cross OVER the standing line. Viewed from above, this forms a clear number '6' geometry. If the working end passes underneath the standing line, the structural lock will fail completely; always ensure it crosses over the top surface.
steps.actionNote: > Checkpoint: Verify the working end rests on top of the standing line to form a clean number 6 shape. This loop serves as the anchor throat distributing tensile force.
svgLabels: FIG. 01 // BOWLINE STEP 1: FORMING THE RABBIT HOLE
Working end crosses OVER standing line
[STEP 1 KEY] Lay working end over standing line to form '6' loop
Working end MUST stay on top of the standing line for structural lock.

steps.title: Step 2: Emerge the Rabbit (Working End) Upwards Through the Rabbit Hole
steps.description: Take the working end (the rabbit) and feed it through the bottom of the rabbit hole, pulling it upwards towards yourself. Pull out at least 15~20cm of slack (the rabbit's head) so you have ample length to circle the tree in the subsequent step without running out of cord. Never push from the top down; doing so creates an unstable slip knot that chokes and fails under tension.
steps.actionNote: > Direction Check: The rabbit must pop out from UNDER to OVER [Bottom ➔ Up], like an animal emerging from a subterranean burrow.
svgLabels: FIG. 02 // BOWLINE STEP 2: EMERGING UPWARD FROM HOLE
Escape upward from bottom of hole
[STEP 2 KEY] Pull rabbit upward from bottom of rabbit hole
Threading top-to-bottom turns it into an accidental slip knot; avoid strictly.

steps.title: Step 3: Route the Rabbit Around the Back of the Standing Tree (Main Line)
steps.description: Lead the protruding rabbit tail around the BACK of the vertical standing line (the tree trunk) in a counter-clockwise sweep. Crossing in front of the tree will ruin the geometry and prevent the friction lock from engaging. Wrapping neatly behind the standing tree creates the signature 'Collar Loop' that grants the Bowline its legendary ability to untie in one second under severe load.
steps.actionNote: > Rear Wrap Rule: The rabbit must pass behind the standing line. Routing across the front prevents friction locking and breaks knot integrity.
svgLabels: FIG. 03 // BOWLINE STEP 3: ROUTING BEHIND THE TREE
[STEP 3 KEY] Rabbit circles around the back of the standing tree
Passing strictly behind creates the critical collar loop for instant release.

steps.title: Step 4: Dive the Rabbit Back Down Into the Original Rabbit Hole
steps.description: Guide the working end (the rabbit) after circling the tree trunk and push it back down into the exact same rabbit hole it originally emerged from. The direction this time is strictly top-to-bottom (Downwards). As the tail passes through the throat, it lies parallel to the strand that emerged in Step 2. This parallel alignment balances internal clamping forces across the knot.
steps.actionNote: > Parallel Strand Check: Ensure both strands inside the rabbit hole lie neatly parallel without crossing or twisting for maximum friction efficiency.
svgLabels: FIG. 04 // BOWLINE STEP 4: RE-ENTERING RABBIT HOLE
Re-enter hole from top to bottom
[STEP 4 KEY] Rabbit dives back down into the rabbit hole
Push tail down through original hole; strands inside must align parallel.

steps.title: Step 5: Lock the Knot Under 4-Way Tension and Master the 1-Second Release
steps.description: Grip the working tail and the right leg of the eye loop together in one hand. With your other hand, firmly grasp the upper standing part and pull in opposite directions with authoritative force. The internal loops cinch down firmly upon each other, creating an immovable lock. The completed loop will not shrink by even a millimeter under heavy strain. When ready to untie, push the rear U-shaped collar loop backwards with your thumb ('Break the Back'); the internal friction collapses instantly, allowing the knot to fall apart in one second without knife cuts.
steps.actionNote: > 1-Second Release Secret: Never pick at the knot with fingernails. Simply identify the U-shaped collar loop behind the knot and snap it backward with your thumb to release instantly.
svgLabels: Push collar loop with thumb for instant release
Hold tail and loop leg in one hand
Constant loop size under heavy load
[STEP 5 KEY] Pull opposite sides to cinch 4-way lock
To untie, snap rear collar ring with thumb; slips loose in 1s without blades.

fatalMistake.title: Fatal Mistake: Leaving the Working End Outside the Loop ('Cowboy Bowline' Defect)
fatalMistake.description: On a properly dressed standard Bowline, the finished tail (working end) MUST sit neatly on the INSIDE of the main loop. If the tail finishes on the outside, it forms an inferior variant (often called the Cowboy Bowline). When hauling gear or pitching shelters in dense woods, an externally exposed tail readily snags on brush, twigs, or rocks, causing the entire knot to unravel catastrophically under load.
fatalMistake.consequence: Consequence: External snagging causes self-untie, resulting in shelter collapse or heavy load drop hazards

shortsScript.hook: Holds a pickup truck without slipping, yet unties in one second with a single thumb flick: The King of Knots, Bowline.
shortsScript.body: If you can only learn one survival knot, this is it. Memorize the 4-step Rabbit and Tree formula: 1, make a loop over the line to create a number 6 rabbit hole. 2, the rabbit pops out from under the hole. 3, wrap around the back of the tall standing tree. 4, dive right back down into the hole. Pull both sides tight, and it locks solid. Even under 500 kilos, the loop size never shrinks. When done, never reach for a knife—just snap the back collar with your thumb, and it slides loose in one second. Keep the tail inside the loop so branches won't snag it.
